ADHD is not one cause: multiple pathways can meet under one diagnosis

ADHD is not the name of one single cause or one biological abnormality. It is a clinical diagnosis defined by persistent inattention, hyperactivity or impulsivity and functional impairment. Symptom data can show common statistical factors, while causal research points to many genetic influences, developmental and environmental factors, and multiple cognitive pathways. Separating symptom factors, risk factors, and a single causal factor makes the concept much clearer.
